benefits: Financing accommodation, on-site catering, and part of travel costs
Rooms and space for meetings in the facility with 2 amphitheaters, meeting rooms equipped for videoconferencing or distant collaborative work and 26 offices to host up to 60 visitors
Support from the IPa team for the budget and registration management, the booking of accommodation, the organization of meetings and social events, and the management of mission fees
Publication of programme outcomes (perspective articles, white papers, lecture notes) in the Institute's proceedings series on request
eligibility: Programmes mainly related to the scientific fields covered by Université Paris-Saclay, from Mathematics to Life Sciences, be they theoretical or experimental
Long-duration thematic programmes, typically 2-3 weeks and up to 6 weeks, favouring brainstorming sessions that lead to innovative advancements
The programme's local organising committee should include at least one scientist from Université Paris-Saclay
Programmes should dedicate a large portion of their time to interactions between small to medium-size groups of researchers, unlike usual congresses
Number of participants between a minimum of 15 and a maximum of 60; programmes with less than 30 or above 40 participants are favoured
Interest in participants staying on site for at least 2 weeks; exceptions must be discussed with the IPa board and explained in the proposal
requirements: Application composed of the programme proposal (5 pages max) AND the summary sheet duly filled (annex 1 of the call framework)
Proposal should be submitted in single PDF-format online
It is strongly recommended that organisers submit a first draft of their proposal to institut-pascal@universite-paris-saclay.fr by 28 October 2026
Interview and selection by the Scientific Council will take place at the end of February / beginning of March 2027
Gender balance in the design of the programme (organising committee, key speakers and participants) should be representative of the field of study and is one of the selection criteria
Co-financing is not mandatory, but organisers are highly encouraged to explore additional sources of funding since the IPa budget is limited
documents: Programme proposal of 5 pages maximum (title, organisers and scientific committee, description of the field and questions, key speakers, week-by-week schedule, expected participation, student and public initiatives, additional funding, stay exceptions, use of videoconferencing equipment, desired dates within 2028 or 2029, suggestions for referees)
Summary sheet (annex 1) duly filled with organisers' names/affiliations/emails, duration in weeks, preferred year (2028 or 2029), participant numbers and estimated co-funding
Both documents merged into a single PDF file uploaded through the online submission form (one file only, 64 MB limit)
For approved travel support, the reimbursement form provided by the Programme Manager with supporting documents, submitted within 10 days after the end of the programme
Acknowledgement in resulting publications: 'This work was made possible by Institut Pascal at Université Paris-Saclay with the support of the program "Investissements d'avenir" ANR-11-IDEX-0003-01'
selection_criteria: Scientific importance of the topic, timeliness, intellectual challenges
Recognized leadership of the programme organizers and participants
Overlap with the research activities carried out in Paris-Saclay
Gender balance in the design of the programme
Expected deliverables at the end of the programme
coverage: Weekday lunches, including one buffet per week
Up to 4000 EUR in travel expenses if needed, favouring participants staying for at least 2 weeks

official.application_route: Organisers apply online through the IPa proposal submission form, uploading one single PDF that merges the 5-page proposal and the annex 1 summary sheet; an early draft by email is strongly recommended
official.study_mode: Programmes are held on site at the Orsay facility, or in an on-site/remote hybrid mode as specified in the proposal
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency rule is published; IPa supports programmes attracting scientists and students from all over the world
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the institute supports programmes attracting scientists and students from all over the world and can host up to 60 international and national visitors
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Programmes mainly in the scientific fields covered by Université Paris-Saclay, from Mathematics to Life Sciences, theoretical or experimental; the local organising committee must include at least one Université Paris-Saclay scientist
official.research_requirement: A 5-page programme proposal describing the field for non-experts, the important questions addressed, key speakers, a week-by-week schedule, expected participation and the use of videoconferencing equipment, plus suggestions for external referees

official.description: Institut Pascal (IPa) promotes thematic programmes to bring scientific communities together and help them explore pioneering ideas and establish new collaborations. Selected programmes are hosted for long durations (typically 2-3 weeks, up to 6 weeks) and receive financing for accommodation, on-site catering and part of travel costs, meeting space in the Orsay facility, and administrative support from the IPa team.
official.region: Europe - France (Institut Pascal, 530 Rue André Rivière, 91400 Orsay, Paris-Saclay)
official.program_type: Call for proposals for thematic scientific programmes (funding for programme organisers)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a call for programme organisers, not an individual scholarship: a team applies to run a multi-week thematic scientific programme at Institut Pascal in Orsay in 2028 or 2029, and only participants of a selected programme are hosted. The published money is programme-level support - accommodation, weekday catering, social events and a travel cap of up to 4000 EUR - not a personal stipend, so organisers must plan co-funding or a self-funded format for everything beyond that. Sending a first draft to the IPa board by 28 October 2026, about three weeks before the deadline, is the highest-value early step because the board gives feedback that improves selection chances, and the Scientific Council interviews follow at the end of February / beginning of March 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research leaders in a Université Paris-Saclay field (mathematics to life sciences) who can convene 15-60 international participants for a 2-6 week brainstorming-style programme in 2028 or 2029 with at least one Paris-Saclay scientist on the organising committee.
application_readiness_checklist: Email a first draft to institut-pascal@universite-paris-saclay.fr by 28 October 2026 to get board feedback before the 20 November deadline
Confirm the local organising committee includes at least one Université Paris-Saclay scientist (2-4 members cutting across the programme's disciplines is encouraged)
Size the programme at 15-60 participants with a week-by-week schedule and state how many participants will request accommodation
Merge the 5-page proposal and the annex 1 summary sheet into ONE PDF (allowed types include pdf, docx, tex, odt; 64 MB limit, one file only)
List key speakers, suggested referees, expected deliverables, and how the videoconferencing equipment will be used
Choose preferred dates within 2028 or 2029 and decide on-site versus on-site/remote hybrid before submitting
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an individual researcher hoping for personal funding - IPa only funds programmes, individuals are invited as participants
No Université Paris-Saclay scientist on the organising committee or weak overlap with Paris-Saclay research activities
A conference-style agenda dominated by one-way presentations instead of small to medium-group interaction
Uploading several files or an oversized/non-compliant document instead of one merged single PDF
A headcount outside the 15-60 window, or a plan that ignores the stated preference for programmes under 30 or above 40 participants
No expected deliverables and no consideration of young scientists, student initiatives or dissemination
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Participants must self-fund anything beyond the covered items: travel above the 4000 EUR programme cap, weekend and personal meals, personal leisure and local transport, and any co-funding the organisers still need to raise. IPa makes no payment advances and reimburses only personal expenses made on the participant's own bank account, with foreign-bank exchange differences and bank fees explicitly excluded, so participants front the cash and claim after the programme.
document_audit: The upload accepts ONE file only with a 64 MB limit; allowed types are tex, txt, rtf, pdf, doc, docx, odt, ppt, pptx, odp, xls, xlsx, ods
The proposal is capped at 5 pages and must be merged with the annex 1 summary sheet before upload - the form has no place to attach the two documents separately

The online form requires the main organiser's name, affiliation and email, programme title, acronym, scientific domain, duration in weeks and preferred year (2028 or 2029), and a simple anti-spam question
Approved travel support is reimbursed only via the form supplied by the Programme Manager, with documents sent within 10 days of the programme's end
Expenses paid by an institution or third party are not reimbursable, and bank fees on foreign-account deposits are never reimbursed
alerts: Hard deadline 20 November 2026, with a strongly recommended first draft by email by 28 October 2026
Selection interviews happen at the end of February / beginning of March 2027 and the funded programmes take place in 2028 or 2029, not in 2027
Participants join only through a selected programme - there is no individual application route into Institut Pascal
Self-funded programmes can be submitted on an ongoing basis directly to the Institut Pascal outside the annual call
The travel cap favours participants staying at least 2 weeks on site, so short residencies weaken the funding case unless justified and discussed with the board
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Draft the 5-page proposal plus annex 1 summary sheet, optionally email a draft for feedback by 28 October 2026, then upload one merged PDF through the online form before 20 November 2026 and await the Scientific Council interview in late February / early March 2027.
